target.title: fix(models): refresh provider auth after CLI login
target.body:
Closes #101254

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who changed model-provider auth while a Gateway was already running could still see the authenticated provider hidden or unavailable in the Control UI model picker until they manually reloaded secrets or restarted the Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

After each successful CLI OAuth, setup-token, pasted-token, or API-key write, the command now makes a best-effort call to the existing `models.authStatus` refresh contract. That contract refreshes the active runtime auth snapshot and invalidates model-auth caches; auth setup still succeeds when no Gateway is reachable.

## User Impact

Newly authenticated models become available to the running Gateway and Control UI immediately, without an undocumented `openclaw secrets reload` recovery step. Offline auth setup behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live Rosita observation on OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (74bb2ad): seven Anthropic models were present but `available: false`; persisted Claude CLI OAuth was valid and direct `claude-haiku-4-5` execution succeeded. `openclaw secrets reload` immediately restored the models in the picker.
- TDD red proof: AWS Crabbox run `run_65fef67ebcb8` failed the four new refresh assertions while the other 35 auth tests passed.
- Focused green proof: AWS Crabbox run `run_0bc8a3488afe` passed all 39 model-auth command tests.
- Adjacent and broad proof: AWS Crabbox run `run_5e2b386e655f` passed scoped formatting, 139 auth/Gateway model tests, full production+test typecheck, lint, dependency/package guards, and runtime-cycle/policy checks.
- Exact current-base proof after rebasing to fresh `upstream/main`: AWS Crabbox run `run_09fa9fbbe5ed` passed scoped formatting and all 139 adjacent tests.
- Structured Codex autoreview: clean, no actionable findings, overall correctness `patch is correct` (0.84 confidence).
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Repository-wide `pnpm format:check` remains red on 191 unrelated upstream files; both touched files pass scoped `oxfmt --check`.

AI-assisted: yes, implemented and reviewed with Codex. No transcript is attached.
